sources.entry: reflex - A framework for building reactive, full-stack web applications entirely with Python.

summary.one_liner: Reflex is a Python library for building full-stack reactive web apps, so developers can write both frontend and backend without JavaScript.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you define a web app's UI and backend logic in pure Python, with state managed in Python classes and event handlers that run on the server. The README shows a `reflex init` and `reflex run` workflow with fast hot refresh on save. A minimal example builds an image generator: a text input, a button wired to an async event handler, and an image element bound to state. The README also mentions an architecture page describing how Reflex works internally. Apps are created as a `rx.App` with pages added via `add_page`.
use_cases: build a full-stack web app without writing JavaScript
prototype an interactive dashboard in Python
create a web UI that calls an AI image model
build a reactive form-driven web tool
deploy a Python web app quickly
scale a Python web prototype into a larger app
notable: Frontend and backend both written in Python, with no JavaScript required
State is a Python class; event handlers update state and the UI reacts
Hot refresh so code changes show up on save
Example uses an async event handler to call an external image model
caveats: The README does not state a license or platform limits
The example depends on the openai package and an API key, which the README implies but does not fully set up
keywords: alternative to react for python developers
